newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss cabinet approves SNB Holocaust compensation.
newsitem.headline: Swiss cabinet approves SNB Holocaust compensation.

text.p: The Swiss cabinet said on Wednesday it approved a plan to allow the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to contribute 100 million Swiss francs ($69.5 million) to a special fund being planned to compensate Holocaust victims.
The decision is also subject to parliamentary approval.
The cabinet recommended such approval should be granted.
A public referendum on the matter is not ruled out.
The SNB's contribution, if approved, would bring the fund to a total of 270 million francs.

The cabinet decision said the SNB's sound monetary policy helped to prevent financial and economic turbulence in Switzerland after World War II. But it also noted the SNB has been criticised for doing gold transactions with the Reichsbank, which was the central bank for Nazi Germany.
The Swiss government agreed in February to jointly administer the fund along with Jewish groups.
Swiss banks also have pledged 100 million francs to the fund, and Swiss industry a further 70 million.
The special fund is separate from a 7.0 billion Swiss franc fund which, if approved, would be created following a revaluation of the SNB's gold reserves.
